claim: Egyptian pharaohs around 3000 BCE collected a fifth (20%) of agricultural production as tax
source_quote: Around three thousand B C E, the pharaohs of Egypt did exactly that, and they called it civilisation.

claim: Tomb paintings at Saqqara show scribes tallying grain while farmers watch
source_quote: Tomb paintings from the Old Kingdom at Saqqara show these scribes tallying grain while farmers watch with expressions that have not changed much in five millennia.

claim: Persia conquered Egypt around 525 BCE
source_quote: Persia conquered Egypt around five twenty-five B C E.

claim: Persian tribute was fixed at 700 talents of silver annually from Egypt
source_quote: They introduced a systematic census and fixed the tribute at seven hundred talents of silver annually from Egypt alone, plus the produce of the fish markets of Lake Moeris.

claim: Cicero was governor of Cilicia in 51-50 BCE
source_quote: Cicero, when he was governor of Cilicia in fifty-one and fifty B C E, wrote extensively about the abuses of the publicani.

claim: Cicero described tax collectors who extracted not merely money but blood from provincials
source_quote: In his letters to Atticus, he described tax collectors who extracted from the provincials not merely money but their blood.

claim: Augustus reformed the tax system around 27 BCE
source_quote: When Augustus reformed the system around twenty-seven B C E, replacing tax farmers with direct imperial officials, he did not do it out of mercy.

claim: Augustus replaced publicani because rapacious collection was causing revolts and declining revenues
source_quote: He did it because the publicani had become so rapacious that provinces were revolting and revenues were actually declining.

claim: Danegeld was first levied in 991 CE to pay Viking raiders
source_quote: Danegeld, literally Danish money, was a land tax first levied in nine ninety-one C E to pay off Viking raiders.

claim: First Danegeld payment was 10,000 pounds of silver
source_quote: King Aethelred the Unready is government collected ten thousand pounds of silver in the first payment.

claim: By 1018, Danegeld had reached 82,500 pounds
source_quote: By ten eighteen, the Danegeld had reached eighty-two thousand five hundred pounds.

claim: Scutage was introduced by Henry I around 1100 CE
source_quote: scutage, introduced by Henry the first around eleven hundred, which let knights pay cash instead of providing military service.

claim: Magna Carta was sealed in 1215
source_quote: The breaking point came in twelve fifteen.

claim: Magna Carta Clause 12 established no scutage or aid may be levied without general consent
source_quote: Magna Carta is Clause twelve remains one of the most consequential sentences in the history of government: no scutage or aid may be levied in our kingdom without its general consent.

claim: English Bill of Rights was passed in 1689
source_quote: This principle was reinforced in sixteen eighty-nine by the English Bill of Rights, Article four

claim: Charles I was executed in 1649
source_quote: Charles the first literally losing his head over it in sixteen forty-nine.

claim: Window tax introduced under William III in 1696
source_quote: Then there is the window tax, introduced under William the third in sixteen ninety-six.

claim: Window tax had exemption for 6 or fewer windows, 4 shillings for 10-19 windows, 8 shillings for 20+ windows
source_quote: Six windows or fewer, you were exempt. Ten to nineteen windows, four shillings. Twenty or more, eight shillings.

claim: Window tax lasted over 150 years
source_quote: The tax persisted for over one hundred fifty years, finally repealed in eighteen fifty-one

claim: Window tax repealed in 1851
source_quote: finally repealed in eighteen fifty-one

claim: First British income tax introduced in 1799 by William Pitt the Younger
source_quote: William Pitt the Younger introduced the first British income tax in seventeen ninety-nine to fund the Napoleonic Wars.

claim: Initial British income tax rate was 10% on incomes above £200
source_quote: The rate was ten percent on incomes above two hundred pounds, with lower bands down to sixty pounds.

claim: First British income tax was repealed in 1816, a year after Waterloo
source_quote: It was repealed in eighteen sixteen, a year after Waterloo

claim: Robert Peel reintroduced income tax in 1842
source_quote: But Robert Peel brought it back in eighteen forty-two to plug a budget deficit.

claim: Peel's income tax rate was 3.2% on incomes above £150
source_quote: The rate was lower, three point two percent on incomes above one hundred fifty pounds

claim: Peel's income tax was introduced as temporary and never repealed
source_quote: and again it was introduced as a temporary measure. It has never been repealed since.

claim: First US federal income tax introduced in 1861 for Civil War, 3% on incomes above $800
source_quote: The first federal income tax was introduced in eighteen sixty-one to fund the Civil War, three percent on incomes above eight hundred dollars.

claim: First US income tax repealed in 1872
source_quote: It was repealed in eighteen seventy-two.

claim: Flat tax struck down by Supreme Court in Pollock v. Farmers' Loan & Trust Co. in 1895
source_quote: A flat tax was briefly reinstated in eighteen ninety-four but struck down by the Supreme Court in Pollock versus Farmers' Loan and Trust Company in eighteen ninety-five

claim: Sixteenth Amendment ratified in 1913
source_quote: This constitutional roadblock was removed by the sixteenth Amendment, ratified in nineteen thirteen.

claim: 1913 income tax was 1% on incomes above $3,000, top rate 7% on incomes above $500,000
source_quote: The initial rate was one percent on incomes above three thousand dollars, with a top rate of seven percent on incomes above five hundred thousand dollars.

claim: Fewer than 2% of households paid the 1913 income tax
source_quote: Fewer than two percent of households paid it.

claim: By 1918, top marginal US income tax rate hit 77%
source_quote: By nineteen eighteen, the top marginal rate hit seventy-seven percent.

claim: Revenue Act of 1918 was supposed to be a war measure but did not end when WWI ended
source_quote: The Revenue Act of nineteen eighteen was supposed to be a war measure. The war ended in November nineteen eighteen. The tax did not.
